endorsements.quote: Phase 3 is a home-based pilot deployment with automated safety monitoring, assessing real-world outcomes such as adverse events, adherence, and usability.

unlisted_practices: Integrate real-time heart rate monitoring into home rehabilitation exergames to adaptively modulate game difficulty or trigger alerts when heart rate exceeds individualised safe thresholds.
Validate wearable-derived heart rate against ECG as the reference standard in stroke survivors, quantifying variability by device model, skin tone, placement, and arrhythmia status.
Validate closed-loop alert logic and latency in healthy subjects before testing in stroke survivors.
Use perceived exertion ratings or kinematic changes as proxies when target heart rate zones are invalid in patients on beta-blockers or with pacemakers.
Review all triggered alerts, system pauses, and patient-reported symptoms within 24 hours by a remote rehabilitation team and classify safety events by severity.
Have a supervising rehabilitation physician set individualised heart rate thresholds before each session based on current medication and clinical status.
Keep real-time safety alert latency below two seconds.

screen.reason: This article is a commentary proposing a framework and validation roadmap for integrating real-time safety monitoring in AI-driven rehabilitation exergames.
